{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Document: 3.1 Term)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings, deviations and negotiation posture

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial architecture is broadly workable — the liability cap is symmetrical, Customer has a one-month convenience termination right, IBM gives a genuine IP indemnity carved out of its cap, and there are no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, non-solicitation or audit obligations imposed on us. Those items are compliant and we are not redlining them.

The issues concentrate in five places, three of which we regard as must-fix:

1. **Customer-side indemnity (§ 8.2)** — § 8.2(a)(3) requires us to indemnify IBM for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", and § 9.2(a) puts that indemnity outside our cap. This is an uncapped indemnity for IBM's own Services and is walk-away territory.
2. **IP in deliverables (§ 7, § 5.4)** — the default for undesignated Materials is Type II (IBM-owned), with a licence back that does not permit modification or sublicensing, and there is no confirmation that we retain rights in our Content and data.
3. **Liability carve-outs (§ 9.1, § 9.2, § 10)** — the cap basis and mutuality meet the fallback, but there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and § 9.1(c)(2) excludes all liability for loss of or damage to our records or data.

Beyond those, we need to cap the open-ended early termination charges (§ 3.4(b)), fix the at-will revocable licence and Affiliate scope (§ 12.1), bring auto-renewal within the fallback (§ 3.2), add a conformance warranty and remedy (§ 5.1/§ 5.4), insert transition assistance and data return at exit (§ 3.5), add mutual assignment rights (§ 14.10), add a New York venue (§ 14.3), and add an insurance clause (§ 14 general provisions).

Two findings did not clear verification and are carried as **needs review** pending confirmation: non-solicitation (§ 14.8) and audit rights (§ 11.3). On the substance recorded, both appear to favour us (no restraint on our hiring; no usage-audit right against us), but we should re-confirm before signing off.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.2 Indemnification by Customer |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action |
| 9 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 14.8 Personnel |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal |
| 13 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 3.5 Effect of Termination |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties |
| 16 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 11.3 Suspected Violations |
| 17 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 14.12 Risk of Loss |

### Proposed positions on the deviations and gaps

- **§ 8.2 (INDEMN).** IBM's IP indemnity in § 8.1 sits at or above our fallback (patent/trademark/copyright/trade secret, standard exclusions, remedies including credit up to 12 months' charges, carved out of IBM's cap under § 9.1(a)) and we are not redlining it; the absence of breach-of-law, data-breach and wilful-misconduct limbs is noted only. On our side, we narrow § 8.2(a)(3) to our breach of applicable law, leaving the Content/AUP and Customer Components limbs intact. The partial relief in § 8.2(c) for IBM's misconduct does not cure the exposure.
- **§ 7 / § 5.4 (IP).** Flip the default for undesignated Materials to Type I (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence back to modification and sublicensing for our business purposes, and add a sentence confirming our ownership of Content and data (§ 14.17 grants only expressly specified licences, so silence leaves ownership unconfirmed). The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials is noted but not flagged — it is not an assignment.
- **§ 9 / § 10 (LOL-CAP).** Cap amount and mutuality left untouched (the absent USD 1,000,000 floor is a sub-element short of preferred only). We add a single mutual "Excluded Claims" paragraph (new § 9.3) covering confidentiality/data and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
- **§ 3.4(b) (LD and T4C).** Cap aggregate early termination charges at three (3) months' recurring Charges for the terminated Services as our sole liability for the termination, and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. We keep the favourable one-month notice period; § 3.3's carve-out (no early termination charges where IBM breached) and § 3.5's accrued-payment obligation are left as-is.
- **§ 12.1 (LICENSE).** Add Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limit revocation to termination for our uncured material breach. Transferability is already satisfied by § 14.10's successor carve-out.
- **§ 3.2 (RENEWAL).** Move to 12-month renewal terms, a 30-day opt-out window, a 60-day IBM reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; fallback offer of a 60-day window with a 5% cap.
- **§ 3.5 (TRANSITION).** Insert six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Content within 30 days and deletion with written certification. § 14.2 already preserves § 3.5 post-termination.
- **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) (WARRANTY).** Add a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty for Materials with a repair / re-performance / refund remedy, and carve the express warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer. The existing care-and-skill language stays.
- **§ 14.10 (ASSIGN).** Add an affiliate/asset-sale carve-out for us and subject IBM's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar. There is no change-of-control provision anywhere, and IBM's subcontracting right in § 14.8 is untouched.
- **§ 14.3 (GOVLAW).** New York law is our preferred position; add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. The mutual jury-trial waiver (§ 14.4) and two-year limitations period (§ 14.14) are noted, not flagged.
- **Insurance.** Insert a short insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) as new § 14.12A; fallback E&O 1M / cyber 2M.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points identified in the findings as walk-away territory. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — uncapped Services Recipient indemnity.** We indemnify IBM for third-party claims "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services", excluded from our cap by § 9.2(a). Uncapped exposure for IBM's own Services.
2. **§ 3.4(b) — uncapped early termination charges.** Amount defined only by open cross-reference to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, neither of which caps it (Attachment A is not in the reviewed document). Unbounded, it could approach or exceed remaining contract value.
3. **§ 12.1 — expressly "revocable" licence with no stated standard.** IBM may withdraw the licence to the Base Components at will.
4. **§ 3.2 — renewal terms "equal in duration to the previous term".** Permits automatic multi-year renewals where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term.
5. **No insurance obligation.** IBM operates the hosting environment and processes personal information on our behalf; the absence of any coverage undertaking is walk-away territory under the rule.
6. **§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — warranty position.** No conformance warranty, no warranty period and no remedy, with all Materials "AS IS" and § 5.1 made exclusive by § 5.2; this approaches the walk-away position for deliverables.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** with the three critical items (§ 8.2, § 7/§ 5.4, new § 9.3) presented as a package and flagged as conditions of signature.
2. **Obtain Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments** and confirm they contain no early termination charge, minimum-volume or shortfall charge, and no renewal price mechanism. Our § 3.4(b) and MINCOMMIT conclusions depend on that diligence.
3. **Confirm the two needs-review findings** — non-solicitation (§ 14.8) and audit (§ 11.3). Verification did not pass, so we should re-run the check before treating either as closed. If § 11.3 is reopened for other reasons, we would additionally seek notice where practicable, investigator confidentiality and no access to our systems beyond what is necessary.
4. **Internal fallback authority.** Confirm the deal team is comfortable with the recorded fallbacks: three-month cap on early termination charges; 60-day renewal window with 5% uplift cap; 90-day transition assistance with export within 30 days; E&O 1M / cyber 2M insurance limits.
5. **Sequence the low-severity items** (§ 14.3 venue, § 14.10 mutuality, § 14.12A insurance) as a single administrative markup to keep the critical negotiation clean.
6. **Internal note only (do not raise):** if IBM later proposes a non-solicit, hold to the fallback — mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, no no-hire."}
